finding: app.js:10 Money total is computed with floats inside render, from unrounded prices, so the total can disagree with the lines shown. Prices are accepted with any number of decimals (app.js:18-19), displayed per line with toFixed(2) (app.js:8), summed unrounded here, and the same unrounded lines are POSTed (app.js:26). The pricing rule lives in the view function with no separate pure function or test. Traced from the JS toFixed spec (ties pick the larger n). Add two lines, each client 'a', qty 1, price 0.125. Each line renders as 1 × 0.13 (toFixed(2) of 0.125 is '0.13'), but the total is (0.125+0.125).toFixed(2) = '0.25', not 0.26. The invoice shows lines that add to 0.26 and a total of 0.25. The server receives price 0.125.

app.js:28 Send has no in-flight guard, no success feedback and does not clear the lines, so one invoice is easily sent twice. app.js:25-28 relies on tooSoon() (guards.js:21), a 1-second timer, not on request state. The button is never disabled. On success the only effect is sentCount += 1, which nothing reads. lines is never cleared and nothing is shown. Driven with Playwright against a local server that delays the first POST by 2 s: clicks at 0 s and 1.5 s produced two POSTs to /api/invoices. Click Send invoice on a slow connection (response takes over 1 s), see nothing happen, click again at 1.1 s: the same invoice is posted twice. After a fast success, nothing says it was sent and the lines stay, so a user who clicks again 1 s later posts a duplicate.

app.js:8 Each line renders as <a href="#"> with a redundant title, which is not a real link target. Keyboard and screen-reader users hear a link that goes nowhere. Activating it navigates to '#' and jumps the page to the top, and the line is announced as a link instead of text. It should be plain text.

escapeHtml doesn't escape quotes (guards.js:4-5, used in app.js:8, bug and security).
It escapes only &, < and >, but its output goes inside title="..." and is assigned through innerHTML.
Any " in the client name ends the attribute early. A name like Acme "West" Ltd breaks the markup, and x" onmouseover="alert(1) injects an event handler.
In this PR the name comes only from the user's own form, so today this is self-XSS. It becomes stored XSS if lines is ever filled from shared data.
The validator for issue 1 couldn't run git diff and read guards.js directly. It judged the bug introduced by this PR because the PR adds the file.

The agents saw other problems and left them out because they depend on input or on the server, which isn't in this PR:

index.html:21 The whole list is re-written on each add, so a screen reader re-announces every line. app.js:7 replaces the full innerHTML on each render, so every li is a new node in a live region. Validation errors, send results and void results are not in any live region. With 10 lines present, adding the 11th makes the screen reader read all 11 rows again. The messages that matter (errors, 'sent') are never announced.

app.js:24 Send invoice posts an empty invoice when no lines were added. The handler (app.js:24-29) never checks lines.length; the button is always enabled (index.html:23). Load the page and click Send invoice. POST /api/invoices is sent with body '[]'.

app.js:26 Send and Void do not handle a failed network call; the user gets no message. Driven with Playwright: with the request aborted, clicking Send raised an uncaught 'Failed to fetch' page error and no alert appeared. The only failure path is !res.ok; fetch rejects on offline/DNS/abort and nothing catches it. The same holds for the void call at app.js:33. User goes offline (or the server drops the connection), clicks Send invoice. The promise rejects, no alert, no text change. The user cannot tell whether the invoice went out and may re-send or assume success.

guards.js:55 Guards are loaded as globals through script tags, with module-level mutable state in lastSend. escapeHtml, canVoid, validQuantity and tooSoon are implicit globals shared by script load order. Reordering the script tags in index.html makes app.js call undefined functions at click time. The guards are also hard to unit-test because lastSend is not resettable.

app.js:24 The send handler is only guarded by a 1-second timer, so a slow request can be sent twice, and a failed send is also blocked for 1 second. The user clicks Send and /api/invoices takes 3 seconds. A second click after 1 second passes tooSoon() and posts the same lines again, creating a duplicate invoice. In the other direction, after a failed send the alert appears and an immediate retry within 1 second is silently ignored because lastSend was already updated. The button is never disabled while the request is in flight.

app.js:25 The send guard is time-based, and lastSend is set before the request outcome is known. fetch rejections are not handled. (a) A send that fails with a 500 and is retried within 1 second is silently dropped by tooSoon, with no feedback. (b) A request that takes longer than 1 second can be sent again, so the same invoice is posted twice. (c) If the network is down, fetch rejects, which gives an unhandled promise rejection and no alert, because only !res.ok is handled. (d) sentCount is incremented but never read.
